why_angle: The cited OREI support pages each list distance by resolution for one OREI kit only. None compares HDBaseT with plain-Cat kits or with J-Tech on the same basis. This page lines up rated 4K60 reach for five kits that all share the same 18 Gbps ceiling (115 ft, 196 ft, 394 ft), points out that J-Tech's 196 ft claim has no stated conditions, and adds each kit's maker-store stock on 2026-11-13. That stock check changes which kits you can actually buy.

page.title: Best HDMI Extender Splitter Over Cat6: 4K60 Reach Compared (2026)
page.h1: Best HDMI extender splitter: which kit carries 4K60 as far as you need
page.desc: Five 1x2 and 1x4 HDMI extender splitters over Cat6 compared on rated 4K60 reach, which is 115 ft to 394 ft at the same 18 Gbps. Also covers cost per TV, power draw and stock on Nov 13, 2026.
page.answer: Short answer. The best HDMI extender splitter over Cat6 is the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K. It is a 1x4 HDBaseT kit with 4K60 rated to 394 ft, 3.4× the 115 ft OREI rates its plain Cat6 kits at the same 18 Gbps. For 2 TVs, its 1x2 twin, the UHD12-EXB400-K, has the same reach.
columns: Link and cable the rating assumes

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • HDBaseT carries 4K60 3.4 times as far. 394 ft ÷ 115 ft = 3.43. Both OREI families use the same 18 Gbps bandwidth, so the extra distance comes from the HDBaseT link, not from a lower-bandwidth signal.
  • For 2 TVs, the HDBaseT kit costs $109.01 more and reaches 279 ft further. $249.00 − $139.99 = $109.01, and 394 ft − 115 ft = 279 ft.
  • Dropping below 4K60 adds distance on the plain Cat6 kits. OREI rates the UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EX115-K at 164 ft at 4K30 and 197 ft at 1080p60, which is 164 − 115 = 49 ft or 197 − 115 = 82 ft more than at 4K60.
  • HDBaseT kits use about twice the power per screen. The UHD14-EXB400-K's 35 W ÷ 4 receivers = 8.75 W, against 8.28 W ÷ 2 = 4.14 W for the UHD12-EX115-K. Both figures are system maximums and include the transmitter.
  • The local loop-out adds a fifth or third screen at no cost. Counting it, the UHD12-EX115-K comes to $139.99 ÷ 3 = $46.66 per screen and the UHD14-EXB400-K to $429.00 ÷ 5 = $85.80.

One distant TV and no splitA point-to-point kit is enough: {buy:avaccess-4kex70-h2-hdbaset-extender} is rated 131 ft at 4K60 4:4:4 over Cat6a/7 and 115 ft over Cat5e/6. It pairs one transmitter with one receiver and has no loop-out.
A 1080p TV mixed with 4K TVsJ-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE, which downscales 4K to 1080p at the receiver (sold out at J-Tech on 2026-11-13). The OREI kits set one EDID for every output and list no downscaling.

Rated 4K60 reach, compared on the same terms

All five kits top out at 18 Gbps, so the distance ratings can be compared directly. OREI gives each of its plain Cat kits three distances: 115 ft at 4K60, 164 ft at 4K30 and 197 ft at 1080p60, all over Cat6, Cat6a or Cat7. Its HDBaseT kits are rated 394 ft at 4K60 and 492 ft at 1080p60 on the same cable.

J-Tech gives one figure for the JTECH-14EX60-AE: 196 ft (60 m) at 4K60 over a single Cat5e or Cat6 cable per receiver. That is 196 ÷ 115 = 1.70 times OREI's 4K60 rating at the same bandwidth, on a lower-grade cable, and it is nearly the same as the distance OREI promises only at 1080p. The JTD-3145 manual's EDID presets include both 4K60 4:2:0 and 4K60 4:4:4, and the manual does not say which one the 196 ft applies to. If your runs are 115 to 196 ft, J-Tech's claim is the only rating that covers 4K60. Only the HDBaseT kits are rated past that.

Only one hands-on test gives a cable length. David Sheneman of The Gadgeteer (March 5, 2023) ran a different kit, the IOGEAR GVE4K60KIT, at 3840×2160 60p over about 150 ft of Cat6, and it held a picture. He saw slight stutter in 4K browser streaming but could not tell whether the extender caused it. That kit ships with one receiver and cascades up to 10. It is listed at $149.95 at iogear.com. His test says nothing about the OREI or J-Tech kits.

Wiring rules matter as much as distance. OREI says every Cat run must go straight from transmitter to receiver, never through a network switch, router or LAN, because these are not AV-over-IP systems. Every kit here mirrors one source to all TVs. None can show different content on different TVs (that needs an HDMI matrix), and none supports 4K at 120 Hz. On the UHD12-EXB400-K, OREI limits Dolby Vision at the remote outputs to 1080p60, while the local loop-out passes 4K60 Dolby Vision.

Not recommended

J-Tech Digital JTECH-14EX60-AE. J-Tech's own store listed it as sold out on 2026-11-13 at $302.49. Its 196 ft at 4K60 rating comes with no chroma or cable-grade conditions, unlike OREI's ratings broken down by resolution. Its one clear advantage is 4K-to-1080p downscaling for mixed TVs. If you need that, check stock before you plan around it. OREI's 1x4 Cat6 UHD14-EX115-K was also unavailable at OREI the same day.
